Leaf.get_bounds() narrowed lb_val/ub_val with integer literals (max(lb_val, 0), min(ub_val, 1)) in the sign- and boolean-attribute branches, so a variable whose only bound came from such an attribute kept an int lb_val and np.array(lb_val) produced an int64 bounds array.

The fix uses float literals so bounds are consistently float-typed at the source; the int64-bound workaround in the COPT NLP interface, which assigned a float infinity sentinel into the array, was dropped.
The COPT PSD bound block is built as CSR, per a review note; the passages do not tie this to a special value.

The int64 bounds symptom appears only when a variable's sole bound comes from a sign or boolean attribute and the bound is kept as an int.
The derivative-check epsilon is a finite-difference step, not a pass/fail tolerance, and no tolerance value is stated for the check.
